# Conservative Party Manifesto 2024 Summary

## Economic Policy

The manifesto outlines plans to reduce National Insurance for employees from 12% to 6% by April 2027, and to abolish the main rate of self-employed National Insurance. Corporation tax would remain unchanged, with full expensing for business investment maintained. The party commits to meeting fiscal rules requiring falling public debt and borrowing below 3% of GDP.

## Taxation and Pensions

A "Triple Lock Plus" would ensure state pensions and the tax-free allowance for pensioners rise annually by the highest of inflation, earnings, or 2.5%. Child Benefit thresholds would shift to household-based assessment, beginning withdrawal at £120,000 combined income.

## Immigration

The manifesto proposes a legal cap on migration with annual parliamentary votes, continuation of the Rwanda deportation scheme for illegal migrants, and reform of asylum treaties. All visa fees would increase, with stricter requirements including health checks for migrants.

## Defence and Foreign Policy

Defence spending would rise to 2.5% of GDP by 2030. The manifesto commits to continued Ukraine support, nuclear deterrent maintenance, and new defence partnerships. A National Defence and Resilience Plan would be created.

## Housing

The party commits to 1.6 million new homes through brownfield development prioritisation, planning reforms, and removing EU nutrient neutrality rules. Stamp Duty abolition for first-time buyers on homes up to £425,000 would continue, alongside a new Help to Buy scheme.

## Public Services

NHS spending would increase above inflation annually, with targets for 92,000 additional nurses and 28,000 doctors. The manifesto includes plans for 50 Community Diagnostic Centres and 250 new or modernised GP surgeries.

## Transport and Infrastructure

£36 billion from cancelled HS2 Phase 2 would fund regional transport, including £8.3 billion for road maintenance. The £2 bus fare cap would continue. Great British Railways would be established.

## Energy and Environment

Annual North Sea oil and gas licensing rounds would continue alongside renewable energy expansion. The manifesto commits to net zero by 2050, new nuclear capacity including Small Modular Reactors, and maintaining the moratorium on fracking.

## Education and Youth

Plans include mandatory National Service for 18-year-olds, 100,000 new apprenticeships, mobile phone bans in schools, and introduction of the Advanced British Standard for 16-19 education.

## Welfare Reform

Reforms targeting disability benefits and work capability assessments aim to save £12 billion annually. Stricter sanctions would apply after 12 months of unemployment.
